title: Beach Holidays in India: How to Choose by Traveller, Budget and Season
seoTitle: Beach Holidays in India: By Traveller, Budget & Season | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Plan a beach holiday in India: the right coast for couples, families, solo travellers and groups, luxury and budget options, trip length and costs.
description: A planning guide to beach holidays in India: which coast suits couples, families, solo travellers and groups, luxury and budget beach holidays, the main types of beach trip (party, quiet, resort, island, heritage, active), how long to stay, what drives the cost, and packing.
dek: The best beach holiday is the one matched to who is travelling and what they want from the days. Here is how to plan one in India.
searchIntent: Plan a beach holiday for a type of traveller

intro: A beach holiday in India can mean very different things: a week in a resort with a pool in south Goa, a backpacker month in Gokarna, an island honeymoon in the Andamans, or a family trip to Puri that mixes the sea with a temple visit. The coast is long and varied enough to fit all of them.

This guide helps you narrow down the choice by who is travelling, budget and style, and covers how long to go for and what affects the cost. For the destinations themselves, see best beach destinations in India.
quickAnswer: For a beach holiday in India, choose by traveller type: couples do well in the Andamans, Lakshadweep, south Goa and Varkala; families in south Goa, Kovalam, Diu, Udupi and Puri; groups in north Goa and Gokarna; solo travellers in Varkala, Gokarna and Arambol. Luxury travellers find the widest choice of resorts in Goa, Kerala and the Andamans. Go between November and March, and allow four to seven nights.
takeaways: Match the coast to the traveller: quiet bays for couples, calm, well-served beaches for families, social towns for groups.
Goa, Kerala and the Andamans have the widest range of stays, from beach huts to luxury resorts.
Budget beach holidays are easiest in Gokarna, Arambol, Varkala, Diu, Puri and the Konkan coast.
Four to seven nights suits most beach holidays; the islands need longer because of transfers.
Prices rise sharply at Christmas and New Year, and fall in the shoulder months.

items.name: Couples
body: Look for quiet bays and good stays: Havelock and Neil in the Andamans, Bangaram and Agatti in Lakshadweep, Palolem, Agonda and Patnem in south Goa, Varkala's cliffs, and estuary resorts at Poovar. Our guide to beach honeymoon destinations goes into more detail.

items.name: Families
body: Choose calm, well-served beaches with lifeguards in season and short transfers: Candolim, Benaulim and Cavelossim in Goa, Kovalam, Diu's Nagoa, Malpe near Udupi, Puri and Rushikonda in Vizag. Resorts with pools make it easier when the sea is rough.

items.name: Solo travellers
body: Beach towns with a social scene and hostels work best: Varkala, Gokarna, Arambol and Anjuna in Goa, and Pondicherry. Stick to well-used beaches and share your plans.

items.name: Groups of friends
body: North Goa (Baga, Anjuna, Vagator), Gokarna and Alibaug suit groups, with villas, water sports and nightlife. Book villas early for long weekends.

items.name: Luxury travellers
body: Goa (especially south Goa and Candolim), Kerala (Kovalam, Poovar, Marari) and the Andamans (Havelock) have the widest choice of high-end beach resorts, many with spas and Ayurveda. Lakshadweep offers exclusive, simpler island stays.

items.name: Budget travellers
body: Beach huts and guesthouses in Gokarna, Arambol and Palolem, homestays on the Konkan coast, and simple stays in Diu, Puri, Digha and Varkala keep costs down. Travel by train where you can.

What drives the cost
paras: We do not quote fixed prices, because they change with season and demand. The main factors are:
list: Season: Christmas and New Year are the most expensive weeks; the shoulder months of October, March and April are cheaper.
Getting there: flights to Port Blair or Agatti, and ferries or permits in the islands, add more than a train to Goa or Puri.
Stay type: beach huts and homestays cost a fraction of beachfront resorts.
Location: beachfront stays and popular beaches cost more than a short walk inland.
Activities: diving courses, private boat trips and spa treatments add up quickly.

sections.heading: Tips for a better beach holiday
list: Stay in one area rather than moving every night; beach transfers eat time.
Check whether your beach has lifeguards in season and whether swimming is allowed.
Book stays and ferries early for December and January.
Plan something beyond the sand: a fort, a temple, a backwater cruise or a food walk.

safety: Swim only at beaches with lifeguards, inside the flagged zone, and never when a red flag is up or during the monsoon.
Keep children within arm's reach in the water; shelving beaches and waves can knock them over.
Rough sea and rip currents are common in the monsoon and on open beaches.
Use licensed water-sports operators and life jackets.
Drink plenty of water; the sun on Indian beaches is strong even in winter.
packing: High-SPF sunscreen, sunglasses and a hat
Light cover-ups and modest clothes for temples and villages
A small dry bag for boat trips

faqs.q: Which is the best place in India for a beach holiday?
faqs.a: Goa for variety, the Andamans for the most beautiful beaches, and Kerala for beaches with backwaters and Ayurveda.

faqs.q: Where can families go for a beach holiday in India?
faqs.a: South Goa, Candolim, Kovalam, Diu, Udupi, Puri and Visakhapatnam.

faqs.q: Which beach destinations are good on a budget?
faqs.a: Gokarna, Arambol, Varkala, Diu, Puri, Digha and the Konkan coast.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for a beach holiday in India?
faqs.a: Four to seven nights for most destinations; five to seven for the Andamans.

faqs.q: When is the best time for a beach holiday in India?
faqs.a: November to March for most of the coast.
